label: Lemma12_Abs_cont

title: Proof
body_md:
For $x \in [0,1)$ let 
$$F(x)= x \, g(x) - \int_0^x |g'(y)| \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} y.$$
The lemma is equivalent to showing that $F(x) \geq 0$. Note that $F(0) = 0$. We claim that $F'(x) \geq 0$ for all $x \in (0,1)$. In fact, by the fundamental theorem of calculus: 
$$F'(x) = g(x) + x g'(x) - |g'(x)|.$$
If $g'(x) \geq 0$, we have $F'(x) \geq 0$ if and only if $ g'(x)\leq  \frac{g(x)}{1-x}$. If $g'(x) \leq 0$, we have $F'(x) \geq 0$ if and only if $g'(x)\geq  \frac{-g(x)}{1+x}$, and these are exactly the conditions in \zcref{20260508_17:06}.

label: coarea
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{coarea}
Let $f\in L^1_\mathrm{loc}(\Omega)$.
Then
\[
\operatorname{Var}_\Omega(f)
=
\int_{-\infty}^\infty
P(\{{\bm{x}}\in\mathbb{R}^d:f({\bm{x}})>t\},\Omega)
\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} t
.
\]

label: radiallydecreasingcomparison
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{radiallydecreasingcomparison}
Let $f,g:\mathbb{R}^d\rightarrow[0,\infty)$ be radially decreasing such that $g\leq f$ and $\lim_{|{\bm{x}}|\rightarrow\infty}f({\bm{x}})=0$.
Then
\[
\operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb{R}^d}(g)
\leq
\operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb{R}^d}(f)
.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For any $t>0$ both $f^{-1}((t,\infty))$ and $g^{-1}((t,\infty))$ are (possibly empty) balls with \(g^{-1}((t,\infty))\subset f^{-1}((t,\infty))\).
Thus \(P(\{{\bm{x}}\in\mathbb{R}^d:g({\bm{x}})>t\},\mathbb{R}^d)\leq P(\{{\bm{x}}\in\mathbb{R}^d:f({\bm{x}})>t\},\mathbb{R}^d)\) and the claim follows from \zcref{coarea}.

label: gradfdisintegrationformulaweak
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\newcommand\mathring\mathring

Let $\bm{\varphi}\in C^1_\mathrm{c}(\{\bm{x}\in\mathbb{R}^d:a<|\bm{x}|<b\},\mathbb{R}^d)$. Denote by $\mathring{\bm{\varphi}}\in C^1_\mathrm{c}(\{\bm{x}\in\mathbb{R}^d:a<|\bm{x}|<b\},\mathbb{R}^d)$ the spherical symmetrization of $\bm{\varphi}$, i.e.\
\[
\mathring{\bm{\varphi}}(\bm{x})
=
\int_{\mathrm{SO}(d)}
R^{-1}\bm{\varphi}(R{\bm{x}})
\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} R
,
\]
where we integrate against the normalized Haar measure on $\mathrm{SO}(d)$, the compact topological group of real orthogonal $d \times d$ matrices with determinant $1$.
Then $\mathring{\bm{\varphi}}$ is spherically symmetric in the sense that for all ${\bm{x}}$ and rotations $R\in\mathrm{SO}(d)$ we have $\mathring{\bm{\varphi}}(R{\bm{x}})=R\mathring{\bm{\varphi}}({\bm{x}})$.
This implies, that for every ${\bm{x}}$, all rotations $R$ that leave ${\bm{x}}$ unchanged also leave $\mathring{\bm{\varphi}}({\bm{x}})$ unchanged.
That means $\mathring{\bm{\varphi}}({\bm{x}})$ is parallel to ${\bm{x}}$, and so there exists $\varphi \in C^1_\mathrm{c}((a,b))$ with
\(
\mathring{\bm{\varphi}}({\bm{x}})= \varphi(|{\bm{x}}|){\bm{x}}/|{\bm{x}}|
.
\)
Let $\bm{\varphi}_{\rho}$ be the radial part of $\bm{\varphi}$, i.e.,\
\(
\bm{\varphi}_{\rho}({\bm{x}})
=
(\bm{\varphi}({\bm{x}})\cdot {\bm{x}})
\frac{{\bm{x}}}{|{\bm{x}}|^2}
\).
We then have $\mathring{\bm{\varphi}_{\rho}}=\mathring{\bm{\varphi}}=(\mathring{\bm{\varphi}})_{\rho}$,  
\[
\operatorname{div}(\bm{\varphi}_{\rho})(x)
=
\frac1{|{\bm{x}}|^d}
\frac\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}{\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} t}(
(t|{\bm{x}}|)^{d-1}
\bm{\varphi}_{\rho}(t{\bm{x}})\cdot{\bm{x}}/|{\bm{x}}|
)\mid_{t=1}
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{div}(\mathring{\bm{\varphi}})({\bm{x}})
=
\operatorname{div}((\mathring{\bm{\varphi}})_{\rho})({\bm{x}})
=
\frac1{|{\bm{x}}|^{d-1}}
\frac\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}{\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} r}(
r^{d-1}
\varphi(r)
)(|{\bm{x}}|)
.
\]

Letting $\bm{e}=(1,0,\ldots,0)\in\mathbb{R}^d$ we have
\begin{align*}
\int_{\partial B(\bm{0},r)}
\operatorname{div}(\bm{\varphi})
\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\mathcal H^{d-1}
&=
\sigma_{d-1}r^{d-1}
\int_{\mathrm{SO}(d)}
\operatorname{div}(\bm{\varphi})(Rr\bm{e})
\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} R\\
& =
\sigma_{d-1}r^{d-1}
\operatorname{div}\left(
\int_{\mathrm{SO}(d)}
R^{-1}\bm{\varphi}(R\cdot)
\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} R
\right)(r\bm{e})
\\
&=
\sigma_{d-1}r^{d-1}
\operatorname{div}(\mathring{\bm{\varphi}})(r \bm{e})
=
\sigma_{d-1}
\frac\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}{\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} r}(
r^{d-1}
\varphi(r)
)
,
\end{align*}
and we obtain
\begin{align*}
\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} f\operatorname{div}(\bm{\varphi})
&=
\int_0^\infty
\int_{\partial B(\bm{0},r)}
f\operatorname{div}(\bm{\varphi})
\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\mathcal H^{d-1}
\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} r
=
\sigma_{d-1}
\int_0^\infty
\widetilde f(r)
\frac\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}{\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} r}(
r^{d-1}\varphi(r)
)
\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} r
.
\end{align*}
Taking the supremum on both sides of the previous display over $\bm{\varphi}\in C^1_\mathrm{c}(\{\bm{x}:a<|\bm{x}|<b\}, \mathbb{R}^d)$ with $\|\bm{\varphi}\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)}\leq1$ concludes the proof,
using \(\| \varphi\|_{L^\infty((a,b))}\leq\|\bm{\varphi}\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)}\leq1\), and that, conversely,
for any given $\psi\in C^1_\mathrm{c}((a,b))$ with $\|\psi\|_{L^\infty((0,\infty))}\leq1$, defining $\bm{\varphi}(\bm{x})=\psi(|\bm{x}|)\bm{x}/|\bm{x}|$ we have 
$\bm{\varphi}\in C^1_\mathrm{c}(\{\bm{x}:a<|\bm{x}|<b\}, \mathbb{R}^d)$, $\|\bm{\varphi}\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)}\leq1$ and $ \varphi=\psi$.

label: weak_definition_weighted
title: Proof
body_md:
\zcref[S]{gradfdisintegrationformulaweak} directly implies the equivalence statement regarding $\mathrm{BV}_\mathrm{loc}$, and it order to prove \zcref{gradfdisintegrationformula} it suffices to show
\begin{equation}
\label{weak_definition_weighted}
\int_{(a,b)}
r^{d-1}
\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}|\widetilde f'|(r)
=
\sup\left\{
\int
\varphi'
\widetilde f
:
\varphi\in C^1_\mathrm{c}((a,b)),\ |\varphi(r)|\leq r^{d-1}
\right\}
.
\end{equation}
First consider $0<a < b<\infty$. Then $\varphi\in C^1_\mathrm{c}((a,b))$ if and only if $r\mapsto\varphi(r)/r^{d-1}\in C^1_\mathrm{c}((a,b))$, and
\[
\int(\varphi(r)/r^{d-1})r^{d-1}\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}{\widetilde f'}(r)
=
\int\varphi'\widetilde f
.
\]
Moreover, $r^{d-1}\widetilde f'(r)\chi_{(a,b)}(r)$ represents a Radon measure, call it $\nu$.
Since $C^1_\mathrm{c}((a,b))$ is dense in $L^1(\nu)$, there exist $\psi_1,\psi_2,\ldots\in C^1_\mathrm{c}((a,b))$ that approximate the Radon-Nikodym derivative $\alpha:=\frac{\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} \nu}{\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} |\nu|}$.
This implies
\(
\int
\psi_k
\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} \nu
\rightarrow
\|\nu\|
.
\)
Moreover, since $|\alpha(x)|=1$ for $\nu$-almost every $x$, the sequence $\{\psi_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ can be taken with \(\|\psi_n\|_{L^\infty((0,\infty))}\leq1\). Thus, taking suprema over $\varphi$ in the previous equality we obtain \zcref{weak_definition_weighted} which finishes the proof. Letting $a \to 0^+$ and $b \to \infty$ yields \zcref{weak_definition_weighted} in these cases as well (possibly with both sides being infinite).

label: radialcharfrepresentative
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{radialcharfrepresentative}
Let $f\in\mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ be a radial characteristic function with $\operatorname{Var}(f)<\infty$.
Then exist $N\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}$ and sequences $\{a_n\}_{-N-1<n\leq0}$ and $\{b_n\}_{-N-1<n\leq0}$, with $0< a_n<b_n<a_{n+1}$ for each $n$, such that $g:\mathbb{R}^d\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ given by
\[
\widetilde g = \sum_{n=-N}^0 \chi_{(a_n, b_n)}
\]
satisfies \(\operatorname{Var}(g)=\operatorname{Var}(f)\) and $\mathrm M f=\mathrm M g$.

label: Prop11_contbv
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{Prop11_contbv}
Let $\varphi\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ be non-negative and let $f\in\mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R})$.
Then, for every $z\in\mathbb{R}$, we have
\[
\mathrm M^s_\varphi f(z)
=
\liminf_{z\neq x\rightarrow z}
\mathrm M^s_\varphi f(x)
.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
It suffices to consider $z=0$.
In general, maximal functions of convolution type are lower semicontinuous, so we have
\[\mathrm M^s_{\varphi}f(0) \leq \liminf_{0\neq x \to 0} \mathrm M^s_{\varphi}f(x).\]
Then it suffices to show that 
\begin{equation}\label{20260508_15:08}
\liminf_{0\neq x \to 0} \mathrm M^s_{\varphi}f(x) \leq \mathrm M^s_{\varphi}f(0).
\end{equation}

Since $f\in\mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R})$ we have $C:=\|f\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)}<\infty$.
Thus, for any $r>0$ and $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$ we have
\begin{equation}
\label{bigr_converge}
\begin{split}
|
f*\varphi_r(x)
-
f*\varphi_r(y)
|
&=
\left|
\int
f(-z)[
\varphi_r(z+x)
-
\varphi_r(z+y)
]
\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} z
\right|
\\
&\leq
C
\int
|
\varphi_r(z+x)
-
\varphi_r(z+y)
|
\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} z
\\
&=
C
\int
|
\varphi(z)
-
\varphi(z+(y-x)/r)
|
\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} y
\\
&\rightarrow0
\qquad
\text{as }
(y-x)/r
\rightarrow0
.
\end{split}
\end{equation}

Let $x_n \rightarrow0$ for which $\mathrm M^{\mathrm s}_\varphi f(x_n)$ converges.
Then there exist $r_n>0$ with
\begin{equation}
\label{good_rn}
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} f*\varphi_{r_n}(x_n)
=
\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty} \mathrm M^s_{\varphi}f(x_n)
.
\end{equation}
We consider the following dichotomy:
\begin{enumerate}
\item
\label{largeradius}
There exist $R>0$ and $x_n\rightarrow0$ for which $\mathrm M^{\mathrm s}_\varphi f(x_n)$ converges, and $r_n\geq R$ such that \zcref{good_rn} holds.
\item
\label{smallradius}
For all $x_n\rightarrow0$ for which $\mathrm M^{\mathrm s}_\varphi f(x_n)$ converges, if $r_n>0$ satisfies \zcref{good_rn} then $r_n\rightarrow0$.
\end{enumerate}
Note that both statements also quantify over the choice $x_n=0$.

Assume \zcref{largeradius} holds.
Then for any other sequence $y_n\rightarrow0$ by \zcref{bigr_converge} we can conclude
\[
\limsup_{n\rightarrow\infty}
\mathrm M^s_{\varphi}f(y_n)
\geq
\limsup_{n\rightarrow\infty}
f*\varphi_{r_n}(y_n)
=
\limsup_{n\rightarrow\infty}
f*\varphi_{r_n}(x_n)
=
\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty} \mathrm M^{\mathrm s}_{\varphi}f(x_n)
.
\]
Taking $y_n\neq0$ realizing $\liminf_{0\neq x \to 0} \mathrm M^s_{\varphi}f(x)$, i.e.
\[
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} \mathrm M^s_{\varphi}f(y_n)
=
\liminf_{0\neq x \to 0} \mathrm M^s_{\varphi}f(x)
,
\]
this implies that also $x_n$ realizes it.
Then taking $y_n=0$ this concludes the proof of \zcref{20260508_15:08} in this case.

It remains to consider \zcref{smallradius}.
Since $f\in\mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R})$ there exists $C\in\mathbb{R}$ such that $f=C\chi_{[0,\infty)}+g$ almost everywhere, where $g$ is continuous in $0$.
By symmetry it suffices to consider $C\geq0$.
Let $x_n\rightarrow0$ and $r_n\rightarrow0$.
Then
\begin{align*}
C\chi_{[0,\infty)}*\varphi_{r_n}(x_n)
&=
C\int_{-\infty}^{x_n/r_n}
\varphi
,&
g*\varphi_{r_n}(x_n)
&\rightarrow
g(0)
.
\end{align*}
In particular taking $x_n=0$ this means
\[
\mathrm M^{\mathrm s}_\varphi f(0)
\geq
g(0)
+
C\int_{-\infty}^0\varphi
.
\]
There exists a sequence $0>x_n\rightarrow0$ for which $\mathrm M^{\mathrm s}_\varphi f(x_n)$ converges and
$0<r_n\rightarrow0$ satisfying \zcref{good_rn}.
Since $\varphi\geq0$, we can conclude
\[
\liminf_{0\neq x\rightarrow0}
\mathrm M^{\mathrm s}_\varphi f(x)
\leq
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}
\mathrm M^{\mathrm s}_\varphi f(x_n)
=
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}
f*\varphi_{r_n}(x_n)
\leq
g(0)
+
C\int_{-\infty}^0\varphi
\leq
\mathrm M^{\mathrm s}_\varphi f(0)
,
\]
which finishes the proof.
